rv.q: Ireland’s play, while it can’t be a roadmap, is a tightly designed, gorgeously felt blueprint.
Delicately directed by Maria Dizzia, the play offers a deep dive into the messy aftermath of domestic violence.
Ireland’s slim but searching play presents an issue of deep discomfort and homes in on the subject of that larger communal response.
Ireland’s debut writing effort—she’s also an actress and fixture of the New York theater scene—is compelling and devastating.
With its sage script and unshakeable leading turn, “Pre-Existing Condition” offers a vital reminder that healing isn’t linear and pain cannot be neatly qualified.
For the most part, Ireland smoothly works such observations, reflections and statistics on domestic violence into the text.

rv.q: Pre-Existing Condition doesn’t give you a traditional narrative or characters–but it gives you searing insight into the way trauma traps the psyche.

But if the power of Dizzia’s staging here feels diluted, Ireland’s play remains a brave and expertly crafted piece of writing.
Its writing, however, while often compelling, is structurally meandering, its central character’s dilemma unfocused, and its ultimate purpose vague.

But there are moments in “Pre-Existing Condition” – moments of fury — that transcend any particular performance, and that defeat the playwright’s apparent effort to make this a study, rather than a howl.
Unfortunately, the temperature of Pre-Existing Condition never rises above a simmer.
Though there are occasional scenes of substance and personality, Pre-Existing Condition, despite its good-faith earnestness, provides little depth to its theatrical world.
Ireland hasn't written a play. 'Pre-Existing Condition' is a P.S.A.
Ireland, who based the play on her own well-publicized experience with an actor-boyfriend during a London production, has written an actorly play that allows its entire cast to shine.
The dramatic tension that Ireland, Dizzia, and their pitch-perfect ensemble of actors are able to sustain for 80 minutes is a rare and remarkable feat.

The subject is heavy and the information important, yet I didn't feel enough emotionally.
Pre-Existing Condition is meticulous about diagnosing what our culture permits, but less adept at letting us sit inside the actual, specific woman living through the realities of domestic violence.
That still holds true, although the play has lost some of its power and intensity with several tweaks and changes.
What she has written is compassionate, intelligent and deliberately unresolved. For me, however, unresolved eventually becomes underwritten.
For now, this challenging drama plays with mixed results.

cn.t: Ireland's searing domestic abuse drama earns strong praise for its nuanced, unflinching portrayal of trauma, though some critics find it too subdued. Nyong'o and the rotating cast deliver powerful performances in this intimate 75-minute work.
